AC5: "The mutation pass copies no nested git checkout: a nested worktree (a `.git` file whose `gitdir:` points at `…/worktrees/…`) and an embedded clone (a `.git` directory) are absent from the scratch copy, while a submodule (a `.git` file pointing at `…/modules/…`) and ordinary directories are copied. · sensitive: revert [verify: exec `bun test src/review/mutate.test.ts`]" -> "The mutation pass copies no linked worktree: a nested directory whose `.git` file points at a linked worktree's git directory (`…/.git/worktrees/…`, also under a path with a `modules` segment, or a git directory holding `commondir`) is absent from the scratch copy, while a submodule (a `.git` file pointing at `…/modules/…`, or a path listed in `.gitmodules`), an embedded clone (a `.git` directory) and ordinary directories are copied as before; the repository's own mutate-scratch is never copied, also with `--scratch tmp`. · sensitive: revert [verify: exec `bun test src/review/mutate.test.ts`]" (Round-1 review of PR 1126: LOGIC-002 and DEG-003 showed an embedded clone or un-absorbed submodule can be a test dependency that base copied, ARCH-001/PERF-004 that a modules path segment let linked worktrees through, LOGIC-001 that tmp mode copied the repo scratch. The skip narrows to linked worktrees, which is what filled the incident checkout.)

AC6: "Failure scenario — a pass removes scratch left by dead passes: under the scratch base, a `keryx-mutate-XXXXXX` directory whose `owner.json` names a dead pid, or that has no owner marker and is older than the stale age, is removed; one owned by a live pid, a fresh unmarked one, and a non-matching name (`keryx-mutate-test-…`) are kept; every new pass writes its own `owner.json`. · sensitive: failure-scenario [verify: exec `bun test src/review/mutate.test.ts`]" -> "Failure scenario — a pass removes scratch left by dead passes and nothing else: under the scratch base (and the repository's own mutate-scratch when the base is elsewhere), a `keryx-mutate-XXXXXX` directory the operator owns is removed when its `owner.json` names a dead pid and was not refreshed for two heartbeats, when its `owner.json` was not refreshed for the stale heartbeat age whatever its pid, or when it has no readable owner marker and is older than the stale age; one with a fresh heartbeat, a fresh unmarked one, one owned by another user, a non-directory and a non-matching name (`keryx-mutate-test-…`) are kept, and a marker that is a FIFO or oversize does not stall the sweep; every pass writes its own `owner.json` and refreshes it while it runs. · sensitive: failure-scenario [verify: exec `bun test src/review/mutate.test.ts`]" (Round-1 review of PR 1126: SEC-001 (the sweep acted on other users' entries and blocked on a FIFO marker), HL-001 and LOGIC-004 (pid-only liveness never ages out under a PID namespace or pid reuse), LOGIC-001 (tmp mode never swept the repo scratch).)
T7: Round-1 review fixes: linked-worktree-only skip, owned and heartbeat-aged sweep, repo scratch excluded in tmp mode, gate test and doc gaps
